parsed.study_design: Single-case mixed-methods study using interviews, focus groups, surveys, and social network analysis
parsed.population_and_sample: Staff of a nonprofit service provider and a retail water utility; 18 participated in interviews/focus groups, including seven interviews and three nonprofit focus groups, and 23 completed the social-network survey (16 nonprofit, 7 utility).
parsed.exposure: A cross-sector partnership between a nonprofit provider and water utility intended to improve hardship-support referrals, information flows, and service eligibility for financially vulnerable utility customers.
parsed.outcome: Organizational network structure, connectedness, trust, collaborative activity, partnership benefits and challenges, and institutional adaptations; no measured household water-access, affordability, continuity, connection, or exclusion outcome.
parsed.rationale: The Methods section (pp. 5–6) identifies staff—not utility customers—as the participants and measures perceptions and interorganizational relationships through interviews, focus groups, surveys, and social network analysis. The Case and Background section (p. 4) explicitly states that future publications will examine client impacts, while this paper reports partnership development and structure. Although the partnership concerns water-bill hardship and referral access, the reported outcomes do not establish an empirical household water-service access or affordability outcome.
